input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

output.company: Revolut (Revolut Group Holdings Ltd, UK-headquartered fintech/neobank group; group-level entity. Regulatory items against named Revolut subsidiaries are labelled by entity)

business.claim: Revolut started as a way for consumers to avoid foreign-exchange fees abroad. By 2026 it was a multi-product retail and business banking app.

Revenue comes from many product lines, including cards, subscriptions, wealth and foreign exchange. Eleven business lines each generated more than $135M in 2025. Crypto trading is offered, including through the Revolut X exchange.
2024 revenue mix: card payments $887M (up 43%), the largest line. Wealth was $647M (up 298%), the second largest.
Business banking was 16% of total income in 2025. Revolut operates in 40 markets.

Revolut Bank UK Ltd left the PRA 'mobilisation' phase on 11 March 2026 and is now a fully licensed UK bank. The 2024 restricted licence had capped total deposits at £50,000. Revolut called the UK its home market.

Geographic expansion (company claim): full banks launched in the UK, Mexico, Australia and New Zealand in 2026. Banking licences secured in France, Colombia and Argentina. European banking covers 30 EEA markets.

On 3 September 2026 the OCC (US bank regulator) gave conditional approval for Revolut Bank US. Conditions: at least $95M paid-in capital and a tier 1 leverage ratio of at least 10% for three years. Federal Reserve and FDIC approvals are still needed, and the retail FX business is excluded. Launch is targeted for 2027.

traction.claim: Company-reported: 68.3M retail customers at end-2025 (up 30%) and 767,000 business customers (up 33%). Customer balances were $67.5bn (up 66%).
Company-reported: about 16M retail customers added in 2025, and $1.7tn transaction volume in 2025.
Company claim: more than 80M global retail customers as of November 2026. Next stated milestone is 100M customers.
Company claim: target of 100M customers by mid-2027, and a long-term goal of 100M+ active customers in 100+ countries.

team.claim: Nik Storonsky is founder and CEO. He founded Revolut Ltd in December 2013 and was previously an equity derivatives trader at Lehman Brothers and at Credit Suisse (until 2013). He held about 29% of the company as of December 2025.

Co-founder Vlad Yatsenko (formerly a Deutsche Bank software engineer) stepped down as CTO on 1 July 2026 and became a non-executive director. Donato Lucia (joined 2018) succeeded him with the title VP of Technology.
Sid Jajodia became global chief banking officer in March 2026. Cetin Duransoy became Revolut US CEO.

Departure: Pierre Decote, head of both risk and compliance, is leaving (reported as 'next August'). David Elwell (ex-HSBC) is the new Chief Compliance Officer and Thomas Wallace (UK Head of Risk) is interim CRO. Single-source report.
Departure: Yana Shkrebenkova stepped down as CEO of Revolut Trading (the FCA-regulated brokerage) and head of UK Wealth & Trading. She had led it since 2023.

Departure: Duncan Batty (ex-M&G), hired in January 2025 to build commercial real estate lending, has left. This was confirmed via Companies House filings and by a Revolut spokesperson. No successor has been named.

funding.claim: November 2026: Revolut confirmed a $115bn valuation after a secondary share sale at about $2,017 per share. Existing employees and investors sold shares, and sources say no new capital was raised. Leads were Glade Brook, Coatue, Durable Capital, T. Rowe Price and Baillie Gifford. Amount not disclosed.
Some coverage calls the November 2026 transaction a 'fundraising', which conflicts with tech.eu's 'secondary' label. The structure was not specified.
Prior valuations: $45bn in 2024 and $75bn in 2025, both from secondary transactions per tech.eu.
A different source describes the October 2025 deal as a $3bn fundraising at a $75bn valuation, which conflicts with the 'secondary' description.
Revolut says an IPO is about two years away. Storonsky has talked about a dual listing in London and on Nasdaq.

financial_signals.claim: Company-reported FY2025: revenue $6.0bn (up 46%), pre-tax profit $2.3bn / £1.7bn (up 57% from £1.09bn), net profit $1.7bn. This is the fifth straight profitable year.
Management projection, reported by TNW: $9B revenue and $3.5B net profit in 2026.
Headcount was about 12,000 worldwide as of March 2026. Revolut plans to add 1,600 roles in India, bringing India to about 5,500, or about 40% of the global workforce, by end-2026.
Company claim: a $13bn investment plan over five years, including $500M for US expansion.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: ECB: in July 2025, Revolut's European banking arm was temporarily barred from launching new products across the EEA until it fixed weaknesses in governance, risk, compliance and legal controls. An independent review of its product approval framework was required. Unnamed sources also reported limits on acquisitions and on onboarding non-European customers. This is based on FT reporting and was not announced publicly. It is unclear whether the restrictions have been lifted.

Italy AGCM (competition authority): about €11.5M in fines. Revolut Securities Europe UAB and Revolut Group Holdings were each fined €5M over misleading 0%-commission trading claims and undisclosed costs. Further findings covered 'aggressive' account suspensions and blocks, and unclear Italian IBAN migration information. Revolut 'strongly disagrees' and will appeal.

Bank of Lithuania: Revolut Bank UAB fined €3.5M after an inspection found failures in monitoring business relationships and transactions, so suspicious transactions were not always identified. No confirmed money laundering was found. Settled under an administrative settlement agreement.

Data breach: Revolut sent customer data, including passport/driver's licence copies, KYC selfies, IBANs and full transaction histories, to a threat actor posing as a government agency. Revolut did not disclose how many customers were affected; ZachXBT suggested high-net-worth users were targeted. Regulators and data protection authorities were notified.
Earlier data breach in September 2022 exposed data of 50,150 customers.
UK licence history: applied in 2021, received a restricted licence in July 2024, and only left mobilisation in March 2026 after a 'protracted tussle' with the PRA.

Sanctions exposure: in November 2025 Revolut was criticised for freezing accounts of Russian expatriates in Europe, which it said EU sanctions required. A 2016 whistleblower complaint to the FCA raised AML/sanctions control concerns; Revolut said these were addressed.

Key-person litigation, not against the company: yacht broker Cecil Wright & Partners is suing Nik Storonsky personally in the London High Court for €17.5M commission on a €350M yacht. His family office calls the claim without merit.

Governance: a December 2025 Companies House filing listed Storonsky as a UAE resident without prior notice to UK regulators. It was later amended back to UK, with the change blamed on an 'administrative error'.

reputation.claim: Which?/FOS data: Revolut had the most UK fraud complaints referred to the Financial Ombudsman. That was 3,242 APP-fraud and 2,631 other fraud complaints in 2024, and 1,875 APP and 1,333 non-APP in January–August 2025. Its 37% non-APP uphold rate was the highest among major firms.

Pattern persists from 2023: the FOS issued 3,458 fraud/scam initial views about Revolut, more than for any other provider. 44% of APP cases and 48% of other fraud cases were upheld for the customer. Revolut cited over 4,000 anti-financial-crime staff.
Critical press, Ireland: a customer in her 70s lost €4,352 in a scam routed through Revolut. Revolut refused to reimburse from its own funds and stood by that decision after media contact.
Italy's regulator called Revolut's account suspension and blocking practices 'aggressive', with no advance notice or adequate help for customers.
Older reports from 2018–2019 described a demanding culture with long hours and high staff turnover. No current employee-review trend could be verified.

red_flags.claim: Supervisory concern over controls: the ECB restricted EEA product launches over governance, risk, compliance and legal weaknesses. It is not confirmed that the restriction has been lifted.
Risk and compliance leadership turnover: the combined risk and compliance chief is leaving and the CRO post is interim, while the ECB remediation is ongoing.
Repeated regulatory penalties: a €3.5M AML fine in Lithuania (2025) and about €11.5M in Italian consumer-protection fines (2026, under appeal).
The September 2026 social-engineering breach exposed KYC documents and full transaction histories. The number of affected customers is undisclosed.
Highest volume of UK ombudsman fraud complaints in both 2024 and 2025.
The $115bn valuation comes from a secondary sale with no reported primary capital or disclosed amount, so it is a weaker price signal than a primary round.

output.verdict: The fundamentals look very strong on company-reported figures: 2025 revenue of $6.0bn (+46%), $2.3bn pre-tax profit, more than 80M retail customers, a full UK banking licence and conditional US charter approval, and a $115bn secondary valuation led by top-tier investors. The areas to examine closely are control and compliance maturity: the ECB product-launch restriction and whether it has been lifted, the turnover in risk and compliance leadership, AML and consumer-protection fines, the 2026 social-engineering data breach, and Revolut's persistent lead in UK ombudsman fraud complaints. Diligence should also test the valuation's reliance on secondary pricing and the key-person and governance questions around the CEO.
missing_fields: Total amount transacted in the November 2026 $115bn secondary sale
Full list of investors and a primary-funding history before 2024 (seed–Series E amounts and dates)
Audited 2025 annual report (revolut.com newsroom and annual report pages returned 403; 2025 figures taken from CNBC/CoinDesk reporting of company results)
2025 revenue breakdown by product line (interest, subscriptions, FX, wealth, crypto amounts)
Headcount trend from a company or registry source beyond the March 2026 ~12,000 figure; third-party trackers (Revelio, LeadIQ) were not opened
Employee review ratings and trend (Glassdoor pages returned 401/403)
Current status of the ECB product-launch restriction (lifted or not)
Number of customers affected by the September 2026 data breach and any regulator follow-up
Outcome of the appeal of the Italian AGCM fine
Other litigation not opened/verified: UK card-fee-cap judicial review (Jan 2026), Allianz Worldwide Partners contract claim, US biometric-data (Illinois) suit
Court docket and regulator-register checks (FCA register, Companies House filings, PACER) were not directly opened
Confirmed effective dates for the Elwell/Wallace appointments and Decote's exit (single source)
